% The whole theme: the scales, their steps, and what names each step.
%
% Nothing on this page is written here. tex/tikz-tensors-palette.tex is
% generated by scripts/theme.py out of theme/tokens.toml and holds the scales,
% the steps, the hex, the roles and the count; this file is the layout and
% nothing else. That is the point: a chart whose captions are typed beside the
% thing they describe can say a colour carries something it does not, or miss
% something it does, and the reader has no way to tell. Generated, it can only
% say what the table assigns, and `scripts/theme.py --check` fails in CI if the
% two drift apart.
%
% The codes are scales, not loose colours: each runs light to dark in three
% steps, and that ordering is the thing being specified. A pair that should read
% as a pair takes the same step on two scales -- canl and canr at step 1, edge
% and edgec at step 3 -- and a figure that needs a stronger or weaker version of
% a colour moves along its own scale rather than reaching for a new one.
%
% Each row is a scale, the bar mixed step to step so the direction is visible.
% Under each step: its name, its hex, the figure styles that name it, and the
% page tokens that name it, by mode. A page token is a tint or a shade of the
% step rather than the step itself, because a page has a background and body
% text and a step does not always clear the contrast a reader needs;
% theme/tokens.toml records the mix and the ratio it measures.
%
% A step that nothing names is left blank, and the count at the foot says how
% many those are. `color=` and not a bare option, because several step names are
% also styles (coef, centre, mpo, gate): TikZ resolves an option as a key first,
% so \fill[gate] fills with the style.
\documentclass[border=4pt]{standalone}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{tikz-tensors}
\input{tikz-tensors-palette}
\begin{document}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm, y=1cm]
  \def\chip{0.62}
  \def\pitch{2.75}

  % the scales themselves, step 1 through step 2 to step 3
  \foreach \one/\two/\three/\name/\r in \tnpalettescales {
    \foreach \p [count=\i from 0] in {100,83,67,50,33,17}
      \fill[color=\one!\p!\two] (\i*\chip,-\r*\pitch) rectangle ++(\chip+0.01,0.56);
    \foreach \p [count=\i from 6] in {100,83,67,50,33,17,0}
      \fill[color=\two!\p!\three] (\i*\chip,-\r*\pitch) rectangle ++(\chip+0.01,0.56);
    \node[anchor=east, font=\scriptsize, text=ttmuted]
      at (-0.18,-\r*\pitch+0.28) {\name};
  }

  % every step, named by what the table says names it
  \foreach \step/\hex/\fig/\page/\x/\r in \tnpalette {
    \node[anchor=north west, font=\scriptsize, text=ttfg]
      at (\x*\chip,-\r*\pitch-0.10) {\step};
    \node[anchor=north west, font=\ttfamily\scriptsize, text=ttmuted]
      at (\x*\chip,-\r*\pitch-0.46) {\hex};
    \node[anchor=north west, font=\scriptsize, text=ttfg,    align=left]
      at (\x*\chip,-\r*\pitch-0.86) {\fig};
    \node[anchor=north west, font=\scriptsize, text=ttmuted, align=left]
      at (\x*\chip,-\r*\pitch-1.22) {\page};
  }

  % the count, so the length of the chart is not read as the size of the theme
  \node[anchor=north west, font=\scriptsize, text=ttmuted, align=left,
        text width=11.5cm] at (0,-5*\pitch-1.85) {\tnpalettecount};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
